text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

SOYBEAN SALE - South Korea's Sam Yang Foods Co Ltd said it bought 16,000 tonnes of U.S. No 2 soybean at basis over November futures on the Chicago Board of Trade. The official did not give further details such as price and arrival date.

SOYBEAN SALE - Malaysia and Indonesia bought a combined total of 60,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans for January/February shipment. The beans were reported to have been sold at around $315-$325 a tonne C and F, Singapore traders said.

WHEAT TENDER - Jordan announced a snap tender to buy 150,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat which is to be delivered in three lots of 50,000 tonnes each in November, December and January. October 15 was set for bid deadline.
WHEAT TENDER - Algeria has launched a tender for the import of 100,000 tonnes of U.S. and/or Canadian durum wheat for shipment in December, European grain traders said. The

results of the tender launched on October 7 are expected later this week. Algeria is seeking 50,000 tonnes of durum wheat for shipment in the first half of December and another 50,000 tonnes for shipment in the second half of December.

WHEAT TENDERS - The Taiwan Flour Mills Association will tender on Friday for two shipments totalling 60,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat, traders said. The shipments contain Dark Northern Spring (DNS), Hard Red Winter (HRW) and White Wheat (WW) and are slated for delivery from the Pacific Northwest.

- The CCC said it is retendering for up to 35,000 tonnes U.S. No.2 or better hard red winter, soft white or soft red winter wheat for donation to Eritrea. Shipment was slated for Oct 30-Nov 25. Offers must be due by October 15.
- Sri Lanka is to seek October 18 100,000 tonnes optional-origin wheat for Nov 11-20 shipment.

WHEAT TENDER cont'd - Armenia will be seeking 21,000 tonnes optional origin wheat for up to November 20 shipment, its U.S. export agent said. The wheat would come from the European Community, Ukraine or if U.S. origin, only hard red winter no.2. The date for offers was Oct 14, Yerevan, Armenia.

- The Cyprus Grain Commission invited tenders for a combined cargo of 12,000 tonnes of U.S. or Canadian spring wheat and 6,000 tonnes of U.S. or Canadian durum wheat. The tender closes October 15 and shipment is November 15-30.

SOYBEAN TENDER - South Korea's Sam Yang Foods Co Ltd said it will buy 16,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 soybean by the end of this week. Shipment would be set for early November from the U.S. Gulf to South Korea's western port of Inchon.

MARKET TALK - U.S. Agriculture Department Thursday said China bought 55,000 tonnes U.S. soybeans in the week ended Oct 3. In its weekly export sales report, USDA said China also purchased 50,000 tonnes soymeal in the week.

... Soybean and soymeal exports in Thursday's U.S. Agriculture Department sales report fell short of estimates that circulated in U.S. oilseed markets this week but still reflected an active sales pace. The sales were " disappointing compared to expectations," said Charlie Sernatinger, analyst with Man International. "The market was looking for close to a million tonnes of new soybean sales and a third of a million on soymeal." USDA reported net soybean sales of 582,400 tonnes during the week ended October 3 and soymeal sales of 248,800 tonnes.
